I try to defuse the confusion over China's export quota system in this podcast. 

In summary, YTD actuals are about 64% of the total clean product export quota. 

However because of the US-Iran war, a monthly quota has also been introduced. Oct is around 500 kt lower than Sep.

Nov and Dec volumes can be huge IF Beijing allows the quota-holders to max out their yearly allocation but I am not holding my breath over this as geopolitical tensions remain high.

FT:

The US is preparing for a protracted conflict with Iran, even as the Trump administration hopes its bombing campaigns and economic sanctions will force major concessions from the Islamic Republic.  

Mike Waltz, Donald Trump’s ambassador to the UN, acknowledged that a year from now the US could still be mired in a stalemate with Iran, without a deal on Tehran’s nuclear programme or a return to prewar shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.  

“I’m not going to put out hypotheticals. One would hope that they’ll come to the table in a meaningful way before that,” Waltz told the FT in an interview.  

But “the president and the US Navy can maintain this blockade [on Iranian ports] for the foreseeable future,” he said, and the administration is “tightening” its economic pressure campaign.

#Commodities

Brent #crudeoil trades above USD 114 and is heading for a third consecutive weekly gain as intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia raise the risk of wider Middle East supply disruptions. Iran-backed Houthi militants have claimed responsibility for recent attacks on the Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu, as well as deadly strikes on an oil field and airport in the kingdom. Meanwhile, the New York Times reported this week that the US and Israel have developed plans for renewed strikes against Iran following the US midterm elections early next month. WTI trades firmer at USD 100.50, leaving the Brent premium near USD 13.60.

Precious metals: Spot #gold dipped below USD 4,000 during the Asian session as momentum-driven and technical selling accelerated following Thursday's break below support around USD 4,060, triggering further long liquidation. For now, the inflationary impact of rising energy prices continues to outweigh support from safe-haven demand and the short-covering-driven rally in bonds. #Silver has fallen to an 11-month low near USD 54, while the gold-silver ratio has climbed to an 11-month high above 74, highlighting silver's relative weakness.

HG #copper trades near USD 6.46 per pound after breaking below support around USD 6.52 on Thursday and is heading for its third weekly decline in four weeks. The AI-led equity selloff has weighed on short-term risk appetite, partly reflecting concerns that a slowdown in data centre investment could weaken future copper demand. Additional uncertainty surrounds whether Washington will refrain from imposing tariffs on refined copper imports. Such a decision could potentially release some of the substantial copper inventories accumulated in the US back into the global market, easing to supply tightness elsewhere.

The BCOM Total Return Index is heading for a modest weekly loss but remains up more than 34% year-to-date. The energy sector is once again doing the heavy lifting, led by gasoil and Brent, while all other sectors are trading lower. Losses are led by precious metals, with silver down 5.5%, and grains, where wheat has slumped 5%. Meanwhile, performance across industrial metals and softs is mixed, with copper and sugar declining while most other commodities have gained, most notably nickel and coffee.

AI jitters hit copper, Middle East tensions lift oil, and gold struggles despite ETF inflows. Meanwhile, grains unwind crowded longs. Why commodities remain attractive as a portfolio hedge, with supply risks and positive roll returns in focus.

The South American nation of Guyana first began exporting crude oil in January 2020. Production takes place offshore at four locations, with a fifth about to be introduced.

Exports are stated in thousands of barrels per day:

2020: 76
2021: 106
2022: 267
2023: 381
2024: 599
2025: 706
2026: 879

Top destinations are USA (28%), Netherlands (20%), Italy (7%), Spain (6%) and UK (5%), but there are nearly three dozen nations on the list.
